items.title: Intuitive wins CE mark for transvaginal gynaecological procedures on da Vinci SP
items.summary: Intuitive announced on 14 September 2026 that the da Vinci SP single-port system has received CE mark approval for transvaginal gynaecological procedures, which the company describes as a world-first indication for the SP platform.

items.title: Physical activity may improve quality of life during menopause
items.summary: Physical activity can raise mood levels and improve overall quality of life for women during menopause, a study has found.

items.title: HPV vaccination before pregnancy linked with reduced preterm birth
items.summary: A study has found benefits of HPV vaccination that extend beyond cancer prevention to reduced risk of adverse outcomes in pregnancy. The Swedish analysis showed having a human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine before pregnancy is associated with a lower risk of major pregnancy complications including preterm birth.

items.title: Menopause supplements an overpriced ‘wild west’, analysis finds
items.summary: Many supplements marketed at perimenopausal and menopausal women are severely overpriced and lack meaningful doses of recommended nutrients, an analysis by Which? has found.

items.title: Cervical cancer screening – a practical guide for nurses in primary care
items.summary: Lead nurse at The Eve Appeal charity Helen Hyndman explains the key principles and practical steps involved in the national cervical cancer screening programme, and how nurses in primary care can support with improving uptake. Read the full CPD module on Nursing in Practice 365 today.

items.title: HPV vaccination protects against preterm birth
items.summary: Women who received the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination before becoming pregnant are less likely to experience preterm birth, according to new research.

items.title: Practice nurses invited to help test cervical screening system changes
items.summary: Practice nurses are being invited to take part in research to help shape changes to the Cervical Screening Management System (CSMS). NHS England is looking for nurses and administrative staff who work with CSMS prior notification or non-responder lists to test new screens and processes.

items.title: HRT ‘ups higher clot risk’ in legs or lungs regardless of dose or duration
items.summary: Current use of oral menopausal hormone therapy – better known as hormone replacement therapy (HRT) – is linked with an increased risk of blood clots in legs or lungs, a study has found.

items.title: Womb cancer tests could be used in primary care
items.summary: A test to rule out womb cancer in women who experience bleeding after menopause could be used in primary care, a study has found. items.title: NICE backs endometriosis saliva test for use in primary care
items.summary: A non-invasive saliva test to help diagnose endometriosis earlier is being recommended for use in primary care, under updated draft guidance from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE).

items.title: Hologic wins £120k Sonata Fibroid Ablation device order for Glan Clwyd Hospital
items.summary: Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board has purchased a Sonata Fibroid Ablation Device from Hologic Ltd for Glan Clwyd Hospital, awarded via the NHS Supply Chain Dynamic Purchasing System for Medical Technology Innovation.

items.title: New method could make IUD insertion less painful, study finds
items.summary: A new method involving local anaesthesia in the uterus could reduce pain during IUD insertion, a new study has found. The study, conducted by the Karolinska Institutet and published in the journal JAMA, found that the method increased the number of women who described pain during the procedure as ‘tolerable’.

items.title: NICE set to back future use of saliva test for endometriosis
items.summary: A saliva-based test that can be used in general practice settings to help diagnose endometriosis more quickly looks set to be included in national guidelines on the condition next year.

items.title: Women posing as men to access testosterone treatment for menopause online
items.summary: Women have been posing as men online to buy testosterone because they cannot access prescriptions on the NHS, a doctor has warned.
